{{alias}}( order, uplo, N, NB, KB, A, LDA, IPIV, W, LDW )
    Computes a partial symmetric indefinite Bunch-Kaufman factorization.

    Returns numeric INFO and writes a separate column count to KB[0]. A
    positive INFO marks the first encountered exactly-zero D diagonal,
    using its global 1-based index. The singular panel still completes.

    KB=N if N<=NB, and KB=NB or NB-1 otherwise. Upper storage writes only
    the last KB pivot positions; lower storage only the first KB. Other
    pivot positions remain unchanged. Incoming pivots are not input.
    Produced ordinary pivots are signed and 1-based; equal adjacent
    negative values identify a 2x2 block. They are not rook pivots.

    Only the selected triangle of A is read or modified. The other triangle,
    padding and guards are preserved. W is output scratch. Prior contents
    do not affect defined results; unwritten cells remain unchanged and
    unspecified as numerical outputs. Finite stored-triangle inputs define
    the reference-comparison domain; active nonfinite inputs have no
    universal factorization guarantee.

    For N>0, full A/W views must be injective and in bounds. All four active
    indexed-byte envelopes must be pairwise disjoint, even if interleaved
    slots differ. Disjoint views of one ordinary ArrayBuffer are allowed.
    Active typed arrays require intrinsic ordinary ArrayBuffer backing.
    SharedArrayBuffer-backed views, including shared storage returned by
    structuredClone, are rejected before routine-owned writes. Shadowed
    buffer properties do not change this rule. Foreign-addon externally
    aliased ordinary buffers are outside the caller contract.

    For N=0, scalar checks and active KB checks still run. The routine
    writes KB[0]=0 and returns 0 without accessing A, IPIV or W. Inactive
    storage aliased to KB can observe its backing-byte change. This safe
    empty behavior is package-defined, not original-reference parity.
    Invalid selectors/types throw TypeError; invalid dimensions, active
    metadata, bounds, collisions or aliases throw RangeError before writes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string|number
        Storage layout: 'row-major' (101) or 'column-major' (102).

    uplo: string|number
        Stored triangle: 'upper' (121) or 'lower' (122).

    N: integer
        Nonnegative safe integer matrix order, at most 2147483647.

    NB: integer
        Safe integer panel width from 2 to 2147483647; may exceed N.

    KB: Int32Array
        One active output scalar at index zero.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output N-by-N matrix view.

    LDA: integer
        Matrix leading dimension, at least max(1,N), even for N=0.

    IPIV: Int32Array
        N pivot output slots; only the factored prefix/suffix is written.

    W: Float64Array
        Mutable N-by-NB output scratch view.

    LDW: integer
        At least max(1,N) column-major or NB row-major, even for N=0.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero normally or a positive singular diagonal index.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 0, 4, 999, 0 ] );
    > var W = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 4 );
    > var P = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 2 );
    > var KB = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( 1 );
    > {{alias}}( 'row-major', 'upper', 2, 2, KB, A, 2, P, W, 2 )
    0
    > KB
    <Int32Array>[ 2 ]
    > P
    <Int32Array>[ -1, -1 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray(uplo,N,NB,KB,ok,A,sa1,sa2,oa,IPIV,sp,op,W,sw1,sw2,ow)
    Computes a partial factorization with alternative indexing semantics.

    Strides and offsets are in elements relative to each typed-array view.
    Positive and negative independent strides are supported. Matrix A has
    shape N-by-N; W has shape N-by-NB. Both full views must be injective.
    Mutable zero strides are invalid for axes of extent greater than one.
    All active metadata and index arithmetic must use exact safe integers.

    The same pivot, scratch, backing and envelope rules apply. For N=0,
    after validating uplo, N, NB and active KB/ok, write KB[ok]=0 and return
    0. No A/IPIV/W or unused stride/offset argument is accessed. Only KB
    remains active; inactive aliases can observe that scalar write.

    Parameters
    ----------
    uplo: string|number
        Stored triangle: 'upper' (121) or 'lower' (122).

    N: integer
        Nonnegative safe integer matrix order, at most 2147483647.

    NB: integer
        Safe integer panel width from 2 to 2147483647.

    KB: Int32Array
        Array containing the one active output count scalar.

    ok: integer
        Index of the output scalar in KB.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output N-by-N matrix.

    sa1: integer
        Matrix row stride.

    sa2: integer
        Matrix column stride.

    oa: integer
        Starting index for A.

    IPIV: Int32Array
        Signed 1-based ordinary pivot outputs.

    sp: integer
        Pivot stride.

    op: integer
        Starting pivot index.

    W: Float64Array
        Mutable N-by-NB output scratch.

    sw1: integer
        Scratch row stride.

    sw2: integer
        Scratch column stride.

    ow: integer
        Starting scratch index.

    Returns
    -------
    info: number
        Zero normally or a positive singular diagonal index.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 9, 0, 9 ] );
    > var W = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 4 );
    > var P = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( [ 8, 0, 8 ] );
    > var KB = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/int32}}( [ 7, 9, 7 ] );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray('upper',1,2,KB,1,A,1,1,1,P,1,1,W,2,1,1)
    1
    > KB
    <Int32Array>[ 7, 1, 7 ]
    > P
    <Int32Array>[ 8, 1, 8 ]

    See Also
    --------
